title: Finger-prick blood test
what: A nurse makes a tiny prick on your fingertip and collects a few drops of blood. This is used for simple tests that need only a little blood.
why: For a complete blood count, blood sugar, in children, and when blood is hard to take from a vein.
tell_doctor: If you ever felt unwell during a blood test
If you have diabetes and are having your sugar tested

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: For blood sugar and many other tests, fast for 8 to 12 hours. Water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Hands
prepare.text: Come with warm hands. If they are cold, hold them under warm water. The blood will flow more easily.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. If you take medicines in the morning, ask your doctor whether to take them before or after the test.

bring: Your referral or list of tests
steps: You sit down and rest your hand on the table
Your finger is cleaned with antiseptic
A quick prick on the side of the fingertip with a single-use lancet
The first drop is wiped away, and the next drops go into a tube
A cotton pad is pressed on your finger
feel: Your finger may ache a little for a couple of hours
after: Keep the cotton pad pressed for 2 to 3 minutes
Results usually come the same day or the next. The lab will tell you when

faq.q: Which is more accurate, blood from a finger or a vein?
faq.a: For most tests, blood from a vein is more accurate. Finger-prick blood is used for simple tests, and it is enough for them.
Usually the ring or middle finger of the hand you use less. In small children, sometimes the heel.

reminders.text: Finger-prick blood test tomorrow. If you need to fast, do not eat after dinner. Water is fine.
